title: METR Secures $71 Million to Scale Independent AI Tests
summary: The nonprofit evaluator will expand research on autonomous capabilities and AI-driven self-improvement while rejecting lab funding.
body:
## A major expansion for independent evaluation

Model Evaluation and Threat Research, or METR, said it secured commitments of about $71 million over the past six months, giving the nonprofit substantially more capacity to examine rapidly advancing AI systems. Announced in a series of posts on August 14, the funding will support a larger team and new projects focused on autonomous capabilities, recursive self-improvement and other risks associated with frontier models.

METR develops evaluations that measure whether AI agents can complete increasingly long and complex tasks without human intervention. It has also participated in predeployment assessments involving systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta and Amazon. Its work is particularly influential because model developers, policymakers and safety researchers use such evaluations to judge whether new capabilities warrant stronger safeguards.

The organization emphasized that it has not accepted money from frontier AI companies. Labs including OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI have provided model access and inference credits for evaluation work, but METR says those arrangements are separate from financial support. The distinction matters as external evaluators increasingly depend on privileged access to systems built by the same companies they may later criticize.

METR credited institutional and individual supporters, including the Audacious Project, which provided its first institution-scale backing. The announced figure represents funding commitments rather than a conventional venture round, and METR did not publish a detailed allocation schedule.

## Why it matters

Independent evaluation has become a bottleneck as AI agents move from short demonstrations toward sustained software engineering, research and computer-use tasks. A $71 million capital base is unusually large for a specialized nonprofit and could let METR build evaluation infrastructure at a scale closer to that of frontier laboratories. Its refusal of lab funding also establishes a consequential governance test: whether an evaluator can retain technical access, recruit scarce researchers and publish uncomfortable findings without becoming financially dependent on the companies under examination.
title_zh: METR获7100万美元承诺资金，扩充独立AI评测
summary_zh: 这家非营利评测机构将扩大自主能力与AI自我改进研究，并重申不接受前沿模型公司的资金。
body_zh:
## 独立评测机构迎来大规模扩张

模型评估与威胁研究机构 METR 宣布，过去六个月已获得约7100万美元的资金承诺，将据此扩充团队，并启动针对前沿人工智能的新研究项目。该消息于8月14日通过一组官方帖文公布，重点方向包括模型自主能力、递归式自我改进，以及前沿系统可能带来的其他风险。

METR长期研究AI智能体在缺少人工介入的情况下，能否完成持续时间更长、结构更复杂的任务。该机构还曾参与涉及 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google DeepMind、Meta 和亚马逊模型的发布前评估。由于模型开发商、政策制定者和安全研究人员都会参考这类结果，METR的评测已成为判断新能力是否需要更强防护措施的重要依据。

METR特别强调，机构没有接受前沿AI公司的资金。OpenAI、Anthropic和xAI等实验室曾为评测工作提供模型访问权限及推理额度，但METR称，这类技术支持与资金来源相互独立。随着外部评测越来越依赖模型公司开放尚未发布的系统，能否划清这条界线，直接关系到评测结果的公信力。

METR同时感谢包括 Audacious Project 在内的机构和个人支持者；后者曾向其提供第一笔机构级资助。此次披露的是资金承诺总额，并非常规企业融资，METR也没有公布详细的拨款节奏和项目预算。

## 为什么重要

当AI智能体从短时演示走向持续的软件开发、科研和计算机操作任务，独立评测能力正成为行业瓶颈。对一家专业非营利机构而言，7100万美元是相当可观的资金规模，有望让METR建设接近前沿实验室量级的评测基础设施。与此同时，坚持不接受被评测公司的资金，也将带来一场重要的治理检验：METR能否在保持模型访问权、争夺稀缺研究人才的同时，继续公布可能令合作实验室不悦的结论。
